title: Redis Cluster replica repeatedly starts full synchronization and reports master_link_status:down
body: I am deploying a Redis Cluster, and individual replica nodes in site2 show master_link_status:down in INFO replication. Their logs repeatedly try partial resynchronization, fall back to receiving a streamed RDB for a full resynchronization, disconnect, and start over. How should I optimize the configuration and troubleshoot this? Do the Redis nodes need more CPU or memory?

symptoms_visible: Some replica nodes in site2 show master_link_status:down.
The replica log repeatedly tries partial resynchronization, starts receiving a streamed RDB for a full resynchronization, disconnects, and reconnects to start the process again.
N0.label: N0 repeated replica synchronization reported

symptoms_visible: After I set repl-backlog-size to 10 MB on the master and confirmed that it reads back as 10485760, the replica still shows the same repeated synchronization behavior.
N1_x.label: N1_x larger replication backlog aftermath

symptoms_visible: The replica continues to cycle through synchronization attempts while master_link_status remains down.
N2.label: N2 INFO ALL and runtime collected

symptoms_visible: The repeated synchronization problem appeared on some standby nodes after a failover.
The affected replicas are still unable to maintain their links to the masters.
N3.label: N3 failover history and resource evidence collected

symptoms_visible: After our team changed repl-diskless-sync from no to yes, the replica nodes restored their connections and data replication.
N_terminal.label: terminal replication restored with diskless synchronization

symptoms_visible: After our team changed repl-diskless-sync from no to yes, the replica nodes restored their connections and data replication.
N_terminal_shortcut.label: terminal direct diskless-sync resolution

solution.intent: Increase the master's replication backlog so replicas have a larger window for partial resynchronization.
solution.concrete_example: On the master, set repl-backlog-size to 10mb and confirm the effective value with CONFIG GET repl-backlog-size.

edges.comment: c0-c4, reporter's cluster: the reporter set repl-backlog-size to 10 MB on the master and confirmed 10485760, but the replica continued showing the same synchronization cycle. Redeployment was discussed but not established as necessary.

question_patterns: How long have the Redis instances been running, and which Redis version are they using?
Can you share the instance uptime and Redis version from INFO?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: The cluster had been running for about 21 hours. The master INFO output says Redis 7.0.13 with uptime_in_seconds 75983; the replica is also 7.0.13 and shows uptime_in_days 12.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The instances have been stable for months, no failover or restart occurred, and this began only after a network outage between the sites.
The current master has been running for 20 hours rather than 21, with the same Redis version and synchronization behavior.

question_patterns: Can you share INFO ALL from both the master and the affected replica?
Please paste the master and replica INFO ALL output while the synchronization loop is happening.
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: On the Redis 7.0.13 master, INFO ALL shows sync_full:11807, sync_partial_ok:7, sync_partial_err:11805, rdb_bgsave_in_progress:1, about 2.73G used memory, and a 10 MB replication backlog. On the replica it shows sync_full:21813, sync_partial_ok:11, sync_partial_err:21802 and about 2.66G used memory.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: INFO ALL shows partial synchronizations succeeding, no full synchronizations, no background save activity, and the replica link is normally up.
The counters differ slightly because I captured INFO a few minutes later, but there are still thousands of full and failed partial synchronization attempts.

edges.comment: c5-c8, reporter's master and replica: participant1 requested uptime and INFO ALL from both nodes. The answers preserve the reporter's raw values rather than asserting why synchronization failed.

question_patterns: Was there a failover before these replicas started repeatedly synchronizing?
Did the cluster change masters or perform a failover shortly before this began?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: Yes. A failover was performed before this situation occurred, and afterward the problem appeared on some standby nodes.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: No failover, restart, or master change occurred; the same master and replicas were continuously running when the link began dropping.
There was a planned failover rather than an automatic failover, but the replica problem still began immediately afterward.

question_patterns: What evidence makes you suspect a disk-space or resource problem?
Can you share the resource metric you are using and explain what conclusion you drew from it?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I thought the disk space might not be enough to support generating RDB files, but I'm not sure. Can I draw that conclusion from this picture?

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The filesystem is at 100% usage and the Redis log explicitly says that writing the RDB failed with no space left on device.
The screenshot was taken with a different dashboard theme, but it contains the same metric and values.

edges.comment: c10-c13, reporter's cluster: the reporter confirmed that a failover preceded the issue and attached a screenshot while asking whether it proved disk exhaustion. The reporter did not know the interpretation; identifying used_memory_peak_perc as RAM rather than HDD is engineer-side.

solution.intent: Use diskless full synchronization for these replicas, verify that the replica links and data replication recover, and treat durable crash recovery as a separate RDB/AOF persistence decision.
solution.concrete_example: Set repl-diskless-sync yes on the relevant masters and persist that setting in their Redis configuration. Then verify that a full synchronization completes and INFO replication changes to master_link_status:up. The screenshot's used_memory_peak_perc is a RAM metric, not proof that the disk is full. Diskless replication is not durable persistence: if recovery after all copies crash is required, keep an appropriate RDB snapshot or enable AOF.
solution.inference_hint: The reporter supplied a post-failover history, repeated partial-to-full synchronization logs, large sync failure counters, and an uncertain resource screenshot. Connecting those observations to the incomplete disk-based full-sync path—and recognizing that used_memory_peak_perc measures RAM rather than HDD usage—is engineer analysis. The reporter later corrected the record in c20: the original setting was repl-diskless-sync no, the team changed it to yes, and the replica connections recovered.

edges.comment: c14-c16 and c20, reporter's cluster: participant1 advised enabling diskless synchronization and clarified that the displayed percentage is RAM, not disk usage. The reporter's c9 statement that setting the option to no restored replication was explicitly withdrawn in c20; the accepted outcome is that changing no to yes restored the replica links. The AOF/RDB warning answers the reporter's related durability concern without conflating replication with persistence.

solution.intent: Directly test diskless full synchronization on the masters, verify that replica links recover, and retain separate durable persistence if required.
solution.concrete_example: Enable repl-diskless-sync on the relevant masters, persist the setting, and check whether the replicas complete synchronization and report master_link_status:up. Keep RDB or AOF configured separately if the deployment must recover after every copy crashes.

edges.comment: Shortcut required because the thread's first suggestion—raising repl-backlog-size—was tried and falsified. A correct initial recommendation may test diskless synchronization directly, but it must still require observable verification before declaring resolution.

satisfaction_conditions: Must identify the accepted technical chain: after a failover the affected replicas repeatedly required full synchronization, the disk-based full-sync path with repl-diskless-sync no did not complete, and changing repl-diskless-sync to yes restored replica connections and data replication.

The diagnosis must be grounded in the repeated partial-to-full synchronization logs, the INFO synchronization counters, and the failover history rather than assuming that a large dataset alone requires more CPU or memory.
Must not present increasing repl-backlog-size to 10 MB as the resolution; it was applied on the master and the synchronization loop remained.
Must not claim that the screenshot proves the disk is full: used_memory_peak_perc is a RAM metric, not HDD utilization.
Must distinguish diskless replication synchronization from durable persistence and avoid claiming that it replaces RDB or AOF for recovery after all copies crash.
Must ask the user to verify that synchronization completes and master_link_status becomes up before treating the issue as resolved.

persona_hint.experience_level: Redis cluster operator who can run CONFIG SET and CONFIG GET, collect INFO ALL and server logs, and change deployment configuration, but is uncertain about replication internals and the distinction between RAM, disk space, diskless synchronization, and persistence.
persona_hint.communication_style: Polite and cooperative; posts extensive raw command output, asks practical configuration and data-safety questions, and explicitly corrects an earlier mistaken statement.
